text.p: NationsBank Corp said Friday it had agreed to acquire Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.
The purchase is based on a fixed exchange rate of 0.6525 share of NationsBank common for each share of Boatmen's common, the companies said in a joint statement.
For Boatmen's shareholders, the deal will be structured as a "cash election" merger in which they will have the right to choose to receive either stock or cash.
At least 60 percent of the aggregate purchase price paid to all holders will be in NationsBank common stock. The balance will be paid in either cash or NationsBank common stock, or a mix of the two.
The transaction will be a tax-free exchange for Boatmen's shareholders to the extent they receive shares of NationsBank, the companies said.
The transaction is expected to close in January 1997.
After the merger, NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., will have assets of $230 billion, shareholder equity of $20 billion, and market capitalization of $33 billion.
"The company will have the earnings power to produce nearly $3 billion in net income during 1997, based on current analyst consensus estimates," NationsBank said.

Andrew Craig, chairman and chief executive of St. Louis-based Boatmen's, will be chairman of NationsBank after the merger. Hugh McColl Jr, current NationsBank chairman and chief executive officer, will be CEO after the merger.
NationsBank said it projects $335 million in annual cost savings from the merger, fully realized by 1999.
This represents a reduction in combined expenses of five percent, it said, coming from operational consolidation, delivery system optimization, business line consolidation, and vendor leverage.
NationsBank said it will use purchase accounting for the transaction, basing the purchase price on the fixed exchange rate for NationsBank and Boatmen's stock.

"...We are creating tomorrow's banking company today," McColl said. "In addition, the short-term and long-term earnings potential of our company has been strengthened dramatically, providing increasing financial opportunity for NationsBank shareholders."

The combined company will have a trust and asset management division with $111 billion in assets under discretionary management, making it the sixth-largest bank-owned asset management business in North America, NationsBank said.
The deal will also generate $650 million in annual fees, $23 billion in combined proprietary mutual funds, and a $110 billion mortgage servicing portfolio, it said.
The merger is subject to approval by Boatmen's and NationsBank shareholders and the appropriate regulatory authorities.
